claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 exhibits significant porosity and microstructural defects.
Porosity and microstructural defects in conventional ZrB2 predispose it to hole formation during extended liquid-plating service.
A nanoscale SiC addition can serve as a sintering aid for ZrB2.
Nanoscale SiC will promote formation of a transient liquid phase during ZrB2 sintering at approximately 2000–2100 °C.
The transient liquid phase will enhance mass transport during sintering.
Enhanced mass transport from the transient liquid phase will improve ZrB2 densification.
The SiC-derived transient liquid phase will modify ZrB2 grain-boundary chemistry.
Nanoscale SiC lowers the energy barrier for ZrB2 densification.
The proposed liquid-phase mechanism improves grain packing and reduces residual porosity.
Modified grain-boundary chemistry increases resistance to defect and hole formation in corrosive liquid-plating baths.
SiC-modified ZrB2 sintered at reduced temperature will have lower residual porosity than conventionally sintered undoped ZrB2.
SiC-modified ZrB2 will have higher overall density than conventionally sintered undoped ZrB2.
SiC-modified ZrB2 will have greater mechanical strength than conventionally sintered undoped ZrB2.
SiC-modified ZrB2 will develop fewer holes and show greater durability during prolonged liquid-plating exposure.
The improvements in densification and mechanical performance may depend strongly on SiC concentration and sintering parameters.

contradictions.description: The material is repeatedly described as single-phase ZrB2 even after adding SiC, but the hypothesis does not specify that SiC is fully consumed or otherwise absent as a retained secondary phase. Thus the asserted single-phase status of the modified specimens is not reconciled with the intervention.
